newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pacific Dunlop sees lower 1st half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pacific Dunlop sees lower 1st half.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Friday its first half results will be well below a year ago, but that it still expected an improved result for the full year.

"Results for the current six months will be down considerably against the same period last year because of our decision to shut the Georgia lead smelter to redesign and modify this environmentally advanced plant," chairman John Gough said.
"The smelter has resumed operations and is gradually raising throughput, although it remains well below designed capacity," Gough told the company's annual general meeting.
"Output and performance will improve in the second half," Gough said.
"We are forecasting an improvement in results for this financial year, although the first six months will be well below the comparative period of last year," he said.
Pacific Dunlop said after it released its 1995/96 results in September that it expected an improved trading result for 1996/97.
It reported a net loss of A$132.7 million in 1995/96 after abnormal losses of A$284.55 million.
Gough said all assets and strategies within the company were being re-examined with a view to optimising current performance and improving the capacity of each business to add value for shareholders.
